t: Context Reconstruction Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Context Reconstruction Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Context Reconstruction Engine does and why archives need it. A context reconstruction engine fixes the 'out of context' problem. When a search returns one lonely paragraph, this engine fetches its neighbors — what came before, what came after — and stitches the full picture back together. Every retrieved fact arrives with the context needed to understand it correctly.
demo:
# Context Reconstruction Engine - runnable demo (JAH-ATK176-000001)
RANK = 1
SIG = False
CHUNKS = ['The treaty was drafted in spring.', 'It was signed in June by all parties.', 'Ratification followed in autumn.', 'The archives hold the original.']  # ordered chunk texts
HIT = 2  # retrieved chunk index
def reconstruct(chunks, hit, radius=1):
    lo, hi = max(0, hit-radius), min(len(chunks), hit+radius+1)
    return [(i, chunks[i], "RETRIEVED" if i == hit else "context") for i in range(lo, hi)]
for i, text, role in reconstruct(CHUNKS, HIT):
    tag = ">>>" if role == "RETRIEVED" else "   "
    print("%s [chunk %d | %s] %s" % (tag, i, role, text[:60]))
if RANK >= 2:
    missing = [i for i in (HIT-1, HIT+1) if not 0 <= i < len(CHUNKS)]
    print("neighbor gaps:", missing if missing else "none")
if RANK >= 3:
    print("window: %d chunks around hit %d" % (len(reconstruct(CHUNKS, HIT)), HIT))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CTX-" + "JAH-ATK176-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK176-000001", "OK")
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Context Reconstruction Engine works
title: How the Context Reconstruction Engine works
description: Overview: what the Context Reconstruction Engine does and why archives need it. Real engines store each chunk with its document position and neighbor pointers, so retrieval of chunk 12 can instantly pull chunks 10–14 as a context window. Coreference chains are resolved across the window ('it' in chunk 12 → 'the treaty' in chunk 10), section headings are re-attached as context headers, and provenance notes which parts were retrieved versus reconstructed. The window size adapts: dense technical text gets wider windows than simple lists.

t: How the Context Reconstruction Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Context Reconstruction Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Context Reconstruction Engine does and why archives need it. Real engines store each chunk with its document position and neighbor pointers, so retrieval of chunk 12 can instantly pull chunks 10–14 as a context window. Coreference chains are resolved across the window ('it' in chunk 12 → 'the treaty' in chunk 10), section headings are re-attached as context headers, and provenance notes which parts were retrieved versus reconstructed. The window size adapts: dense technical text gets wider windows than simple lists. Advanced reconstruction ranks neighbor chunks by relevance rather than blindly taking adjacent ones, handles documents where the 'context' lives in a different file (appendices, footnotes), and marks every reconstructed span so downstream users can distinguish retrieved text from re-attached context. Quality is measured by answer correctness with and without reconstruction on QA benchmarks. The limits are fragmented archives where neighbors are genuinely missing — the engine reports the gap instead of inventing continuity.

Advanced reconstruction ranks neighbor chunks by relevance rather than blindly taking adjacent ones, handles documents where the 'context' lives in a different file (appendices, footnotes), and marks every reconstructed span so downstream users can distinguish retrieved text from re-attached context. Quality is measured by answer correctness with and without reconstruction on QA benchmarks. The limits are fragmented archives where neighbors are genuinely missing — the engine reports the gap instead of inventing continuity.

# Context Reconstruction Engine - runnable demo (JAH-ATK176-000015)
RANK = 3
SIG = False
CHUNKS = ['The signal arrived at dawn.', 'It repeated three times.', 'Analysts confirmed the pattern.', 'The log was sealed.']  # ordered chunk texts
HIT = 2  # retrieved chunk index
def reconstruct(chunks, hit, radius=1):
    lo, hi = max(0, hit-radius), min(len(chunks), hit+radius+1)
    return [(i, chunks[i], "RETRIEVED" if i == hit else "context") for i in range(lo, hi)]
for i, text, role in reconstruct(CHUNKS, HIT):
    tag = ">>>" if role == "RETRIEVED" else "   "
    print("%s [chunk %d | %s] %s" % (tag, i, role, text[:60]))
if RANK >= 2:
    missing = [i for i in (HIT-1, HIT+1) if not 0 <= i < len(CHUNKS)]
    print("neighbor gaps:", missing if missing else "none")
if RANK >= 3:
    print("window: %d chunks around hit %d" % (len(reconstruct(CHUNKS, HIT)), HIT))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-CTX-" + "JAH-ATK176-000015")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK176-000015", "OK")
